newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-IRVIN'S LAWYERS SAY COWBOYS STAR IS INNOCENT.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-IRVIN'S LAWYERS SAY COWBOYS STAR IS INNOCENT.

text.p: Lawyers for Dallas Cowboys star Michael Irvin, accused of holding a gun against a woman's head while a teammate raped her, said on Thursday he was not near the alleged crime scene and has witnesses to back him up.

As police said they were still in the early stages of their investigation, attorney Royce West said a security guard will testify, if necessary, that Irvin did not enter teammate Erik Williams' home on Sunday night, when the alleged attack took place.

"I want America to know the security guard will state Michael Irvin never went in that security gate, never went to Erik Williams's house on Sunday night," West told ABC's "Good Morning America" show.

Another of Irvin's lawyers, Anthony Lyons, told the Fort Worth Star Telegram newspaper that the wide receiver spent most of Sunday evening at the Cowboys Sports Cafe near Dallas, and that several people have called to say they saw him there.

A 23-year-old Dallas woman accused Irvin of holding a gun against her head while Williams and an unidentified man raped her inside Williams's home on Sunday night. She said the men videotaped the assault.
Police this week searched Williams's home and seized a videotape showing sexual activity, but said on Thursday no quick arrests should be expected.
"It is going to be days at least, if not weeks, before any determination can be made on whether there is a criminal case to be filed," police spokesman Ed Spencer said on Thursday.
Irvin emphatically denied the allegations and said he was anxious to speak to police.
"I am looking forward to helping and cooperating in any way I can," Irvin told reporters on Wednesday.

Irvin is on probation after pleading no contest to felony cocaine possession charges last year. If arrested on aggravated sexual assault charges, he could have his probation revoked and be sent to jail.

The estranged husband of the woman making the assault allegations said he doubted she was telling the truth. The man told The Dallas Morning News his estranged wife, whose name was not released, twice falsely accused men of sexual assault in the past.
"It seems very reasonable that she is making this up," the man said, although he admitted having no first-hand knowledge of the alleged assault.

The newspaper also interviewed two friends of the woman who said they had no doubt she was sexually assaulted. They said they consoled her after the alleged attack and described her as bruised, distraught and fearful.

The Cowboys were preparing for a second-round playoff game against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. They are the reigning Super Bowl champions, and Irvin and Williams played key roles in the team's three Super Bowl victories over the last four years.
The slow advance of the police investigation suggested the two players would have no problem travelling to Sunday's game in Charlotte, North Carolina.
